coordinates.locator: arXiv:1608.00306, Sec. 3.1; geocode of the plant
coordinates.note: Campus-grade point: the OpenStreetMap land-use polygon of the Kuosheng Nuclear Power Plant (about 300 m across). The laboratory is in the reactor building, 28 m from core #1; no source gives its coordinates, so the point is not relabelled as a detector position.
coordinates.quote: The Kuo-Sheng Reactor Neutrino Laboratory (KSNL) is located at a distance of 28 m from the core #1 of the Kuo-Sheng Nuclear Power Station operated by the Taiwan Power Company at the northern shore of Taiwan.

depth_mwe.note: Concrete of the reactor building; the 2008 paper says 'about 30 meter-water-equivalence'. Located ~12 m below sea level on the first floor of the reactor building.
depth_mwe.quote: The concrete of the reactor building provides 30 meters of water equivalent overburden

name: Kuo-Sheng Nuclear Power Station site (KSNL)
notes: `setting: underground` is a shallow, building-covered location (~12 m below sea level), not a mine or tunnel.

summary.plain: The Kuo-Sheng nuclear power plant on the northern coast of Taiwan, where the TEXONO laboratory sits in the reactor building a few tens of metres from a reactor core.
summary.technical: Kuo-Sheng Nuclear Power Station (Wanli District, New Taipei); KSNL is on the ground floor of the reactor building, 28 m from core #1, ~12 m below sea level (~30 m.w.e.).
